articles.title: Gloucestershire set to change name to Bristol for T20 Blast cricket in bid to boost attendances
articles.summary: Name change will apply to men's and women's teams for T20 cricket; Warwickshire competed as Birmingham Bears from 2014 to 2025 before reverting to traditional county name; Gloucestershire have won the men's Blast once, back in 2024 when they beat Somerset in the final
articles.body:
The club confirmed in a statement that they will be creating a new T20 identity for their men's and women's teams and have made the decision "as part of our wider strategic vision to grow domestic cricket, attract new audiences across the region, and drive commercial reinvestment back into the sport."

The club will continue to operate as Gloucestershire in the County Championship and One Day Cup.

A club statement issued on Friday said: "Over recent months, Gloucestershire County Cricket Club has worked closely with our players, our Members Working Group, the ECB, and a number of key stakeholders to help shape an exciting new chapter in our evolution.

"Building on more than 150 years of proud heritage, Gloucestershire Cricket will always remain our overarching identity and the foundation of everything we do.

"As part of our wider strategic vision to grow domestic cricket, attract new audiences across the region, and drive commercial reinvestment back into the sport, we will be creating a new dedicated T20 identity for our men's and women's teams.

"Full details of our plans and brand identity moving forward will soon be officially unveiled, in alignment with the forthcoming ECB national domestic fixture release.

"We look forward to sharing our complete vision with our fans, partners and media in the near future."

Warwickshire played under the Birmingham Bears moniker in the Blast from 2014, before reverting to their traditional county name ahead of the 2026 campaign.

Gloucestershire have won the men's Blast once in their history, in 2024 when they defeated Somerset in the final.

The county were also runners-up to Kent back in 2007.

Northamptonshire Steelbacks won the men's Blast in 2026, with The Blaze claiming the women's title.

articles.title: Big blow for New Zealand! Star batter ruled out of remainder of ODI series against India
articles.summary: New Zealand have suffered a setback ahead of the second ODI against India, with opener Devon Conway ruled out of the remaining matches of the five-game
articles.body: New Zealand have suffered a setback ahead of the second ODI against India, with opener Devon Conway ruled out of the remaining matches of the five-game series after sustaining a concussion during a training session on Tuesday.Conway suffered the injury while fielding during practice, forcing him out of the remainder of the ODI series. Left-handed batter Nick Kelly, who was initially selected for the fourth and fifth ODIs, will now join the squad in Wellington on Friday as his replacement.There was some relief for the New Zealand camp, however, as Matt Henry, who was involved in the fielding mishap that resulted in Conway's injury, has been cleared of concussion.The development comes after New Zealand lost the opening ODI to India in Auckland on Wednesday. Virat Kohli's authoritative 74, coupled with impressive bowling performances from Arshdeep Singh and Anshul Kamboj, helped India secure a comfortable victory in the rain-affected contest.Arshdeep led the attack with four wickets, while Gurnoor Brar picked up three scalps and Kamboj claimed two as New Zealand were bowled out for 185. India then chased down the revised target of 143 in 32 overs despite rain interruptions.The second ODI will be played at Sky Stadium in Wellington on Saturday, with New Zealand looking to bounce back and level the series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India vs New Zealand: Rain keeps India indoors in Wellington; Siraj selection adds to intrigue
articles.summary: Wellington: Steady drizzle in Wellington on Friday forced New Zealand to shift their training to an indoor facility opposite the Basin Reserve, while
articles.body: Wellington: Steady drizzle in Wellington on Friday forced New Zealand to shift their training to an indoor facility opposite the Basin Reserve, while India cancelled their training session and stayed back at their hotel on the eve of the second ODI of the five-match series on Saturday.The turnaround time between the Auckland and Wellington fixtures permitted only one practice session for both teams following their travel day on November 5. While players who were part of India's T20I set-up have already had a taste of the windy Welly, most will walk straight into action, hoping to acclimatise quickly. New Zealand poses stiff challenges, and the varying ground dimensions and weather conditions across the country present different hurdles to overcome.From the short straight at Eden Park to the shorter square at Hnry Stadium, even the bowlers from both teams will need to make that quick adjustment because what worked in Auckland may or may not reap rewards in Wellington. For Kiwi quick Blair Tickner, it's about getting the work done in whatever time you get and finding the right balance between fixtures."We still do a bit of bowling between. You can't do it every time, there's guys going in and out of the session and we're just balancing that, and a lot of guys going to Test cricket as well, so there's a lot of balance happening. We have a great team and they are all sort of scheduling each bowler where they need to be, so now it's working so far, so good," said Tickner on the cramped schedule."I'm still coming back from a few injuries in the winter, so I'm sort of trying to bowl a bit more. I love bowling, getting that rhythm right, so I'm definitely still bowling in training and getting me to it," added the fast bowler, who flexed his muscles by smashing four massive sixes in Auckland.Tickner enjoyed putting on a show for the crowd but now wants to put up an improved performance with the ball at a venue where Abhishek Sharma blew the hosts away with a 38-ball 113. With lessons learnt, New Zealand will continue to come hard at India, and attack will be the mantra for the hosts."If the perfect plan works out, we are going to be attacking and get early wickets. That's the dream, and every one day team's bowling attack wants to bowl teams out, so we're looking to bowl teams out first before thinking about defensive play. We'll work it out there," said Tickner.Siraj has joined the team and is available for selection, but the management will take a call, whether he will play or not.Mohammed Siraj or Auqib Nabi?India will have to decide whether to bench Nabi to make way for Siraj, who joined the team after finishing his India A duties. The experienced fast bowler linked up with the squad in Wellington and remains available for selection. A practice session could have offered hints about the team management's thinking, but fielding coach Subhadeep Ghosh kept his selection cards close to his chest."Siraj has joined the team and is available for selection, but the management will take a call whether he will play or not," said Ghosh.Given the weather conditions, it looks increasingly difficult for India to alter their bowling combination, and the only toss-up could be between Siraj and Nabi.There is a strong forecast of rain on match day as well, and the fans could be in for another frustrating day of cricket when the two teams take the field.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Aussies turn to 'Mr Cricket': Former CSK coach joins Australia support staff for Ashes and 2027 World Cup
articles.summary: Mike Hussey was on Friday appointed as a consultant coach to the Australian team for next year's Ashes series against England and the 2027 ODI World Cup.
articles.body: Mike Hussey was on Friday appointed as a consultant coach to the Australian team for next year's Ashes series against England and the 2027 ODI World Cup.The former Australia batter had revealed in August that England's new red-ball coach, Stephen Fleming, had informally approached him to take up the role of Test batting mentor. However, the 51-year-old turned down the offer and has instead decided to work with Australia as they look to address their batting struggles, which were exposed during their recent 2-1 Test series defeat in South Africa.Hussey, who earned the nickname 'Mr Cricket' for his technical knowledge of the game, will also assist the Australian coaching staff during this month's home T20 series against England and the subsequent four-Test series against New Zealand.His role will extend beyond next year's assignments, with Hussey also set to work with Australia at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where cricket will feature, and the 2028 T20 World Cup."I am extremely excited about being a part of the team in a more formal and meaningful role in the coming years," said Hussey, who represented Australia in more than 300 international matches across all formats."This team has achieved so much in recent times, to which I hope I can add value to the coaching and playing groups ahead of what will be an exciting and challenging period."Hussey has considerable coaching experience, having worked with both Australia and England. He was part of England's coaching setup when they won the T20 World Cup in 2022 and served as Chennai Super Kings' long-time batting coach under Fleming in the Indian Premier League. He also coached Welsh Fire in this year's edition of The Hundred."Mike has been a highly valued part of our staff in the past and brings a considerable skill set which is complementary to the coaches and players," said Australia head coach Andrew McDonald."Not only is his expertise as a player and coach across multiple formats, competitions, countries invaluable, so are his qualities as a person."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Too early for him’: Sachin Tendulkar's blunt verdict on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s leadership role at 15
articles.summary: At just 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already achieved milestones that remain a distant dream for many cricketers throughout their careers.
articles.body: At just 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already achieved milestones that remain a distant dream for many cricketers throughout their careers. From finishing as the leading run-scorer in an Indian Premier League (IPL) season to smashing a match-winning century in the U-19 World Cup final to clinch the title, the teenager has made remarkable strides in a short span of time.However, his elevation to the role of East Zone vice-captain for the Duleep Trophy did not go down well with everyone. Among those who believe the youngster was handed a leadership responsibility too early is batting legend Sachin Tendulkar.Although Tendulkar had not publicly questioned the selectors' decision at the time of the announcement, he shared his reservations during a Reddit Q&A session, suggesting that Sooryavanshi should focus on gaining more experience in red-ball cricket before taking on such responsibilities.Responding to a fan who asked for his views on the 15-year-old being entrusted with a leadership role, Tendulkar said: "I feel it's too early for him to become a vice-captain in the Duleep Trophy. We have to let him play more matches with the red ball and take one step at a time!"Sooryavanshi had featured in just eight red-ball matches for Bihar before being named East Zone skipper Ishan Kishan's deputy. The decision meant he was preferred over Abhimanyu Easwaran, an experienced campaigner with more than 100 First-Class appearances.The East Zone selection committee subsequently clarified that the appointment was made with the youngster's development in mind and should not be interpreted as an indication of the pecking order within the squad.Sooryavanshi also got a taste of captaincy during the tournament when Kishan was forced to leave the field due to an injury. The teenager stepped in to lead the side and was involved in several important on-field decisions, including DRS calls. Videos of his involvement in those reviews also gained traction on social media.Meanwhile, Sooryavanshi has continued to strengthen his position in India's T20I setup, although he is yet to establish himself as a regular opener. The youngster faces competition for a place in the top three from established names such as Sanju Samson, Abhishek Sharma and Ishan Kishan.Tendulkar names favourite captainsDuring the same interaction, Tendulkar also reflected on his own stint as India's captain, describing the opportunity to lead the national side as a tremendous honour. However, he admitted that the position did not always give him complete control over team selection.Tendulkar, who made his international debut on November 15, 1989, before bringing the curtain down on his career on November 16, 2013, also spoke about the changes in the functioning of Indian cricket over the years."It was a great honour to lead the team as captain. However, I didn’t always have the freedom to pick my team entirely on my own. The BCCI today is a far more professional organisation than it was in the 1990s. Indian cricket also went through a particularly dark phase during that period," Tendulkar said.Asked to name his favourite captains, the former India skipper singled out Sourav Ganguly and MS Dhoni, acknowledging the impact both had on Indian cricket."As far as my favourite captains go, Sourav Ganguly and MS Dhoni would definitely be at the top of my list!!," Tendulkar said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘There was no place for mediocrity’: Venkatesh Iyer reveals Gautam Gambhir's dressing-room rule at KKR
articles.summary: Venkatesh Iyer has opened up about Gautam Gambhir's influence on Kolkata Knight Riders' (KKR) dressing room during their title-winning Indian Premier
articles.body: Venkatesh Iyer has opened up about Gautam Gambhir's influence on Kolkata Knight Riders' (KKR) dressing room during their title-winning Indian Premier League (IPL) 2024 campaign, explaining how the former captain's presence helped establish a culture where players were always ready to attack.Gambhir, who led KKR to IPL titles in 2012 and 2014, returned to the franchise in 2024 as a mentor. His involvement proved important as the team went on to win another championship. He has since moved on from the franchise and is currently serving as India's head coach.Recalling the atmosphere in the KKR dugout, Iyer explained that the team's batting order was always prepared to take the field, even when the openers were still at the crease.“Our two openers, Narine and Salt, would go out to bat. Angkrish would sit there with his pads on. He just sat there, while the rest of us - me, Shreyas, Nitish Rana, Rinku Singh, Ramandeep, and Andre Russell - sat inside; all five of us would be padded up and ready to go from the second over itself,” Iyer said during a podcast with Aakash Chopra.Iyer said there was a sense of competition among the batters, with everyone eager to get an opportunity. However, Sunil Narine and Phil Salt often continued batting for several overs, keeping the waiting players on their toes.“There was this competition; anyone could go in at any moment, boss. We stayed ready, like literally. I, of course, saw it from my own perspective, but looking at them, they were like lions ready to go: ‘Just send us in, we’ll go and...’ And touch wood, Salt and Narine wouldn’t get out, they wouldn’t get out for a long time.”He also recalled how Gambhir would communicate the possible batting combinations from the dugout as the innings progressed. Players had to remain prepared because the instructions could change depending on the situation.“If they didn’t get out for three or four overs, GG sir from over there would say: ‘Angkrish, Venky is going next’, and I’d be ready. If they still didn’t get out for two more overs, he’d say from there: ‘It’s a left-right combination, Venky and Shreyas ’- and both of us would be ready. Then, if they stayed in even longer: ‘Call Russell, tell Russell’; but all of us were raring to go like that.”For Iyer, this was a different kind of dressing-room environment, with every batter looking forward to getting an opportunity to take the attack to the opposition.“That was the first time I witnessed something like that: give us an opportunity and we will go smash it."'There was no place for mediocrity': Iyer on GambhirIyer attributed the team's approach to the confidence Gambhir gave the players. According to him, the mentor's presence meant the batters were not worried about failure, but they also knew that the standards expected of them were high.“He was sitting right behind us. There was no fear. And there was no place for mediocrity in that dressing room. You can’t play a mediocre shot or a false stroke and come sit next to him. You can’t do that.”Iyer clarified that Gambhir did not need to introduce any formal rules to establish this atmosphere. His presence and expectations were enough to influence how the players approached their game.The franchise eventually lifted its third IPL trophy, adding to the titles it had won under Gambhir's captaincy in 2012 and 2014.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Sarfaraz Khan races from first slip to leg slip, dives full length to take a blinder to end 167-run stand as Mumbai turn the tide - Watch
articles.summary: A stunning catch from Sarfaraz Khan helped Mumbai break a 167-run partnership and turn the match on ite head in the final hour as the 42-time champions
articles.body: A stunning catch from Sarfaraz Khan helped Mumbai break a 167-run partnership and turn the match on ite head in the final hour as the 42-time champions defeated Railways by 106 runs in their Ranji Trophy Group D clash on Thursday.Railways were firmly in the contest for much of the final day, thanks to centuries from opener Eshaan Goyal (103) and No. 7 batter Zubair Ali (115). The pair had kept Mumbai waiting for 156 minutes, facing 212 balls and adding 167 runs for the sixth wicket. However, Sarfaraz's effort in the field opened the door for Mumbai, who picked up their fourth outright win of the season to finish the first round with 27 points.Sarfaraz, who had earlier effected a run-out and dropped a catch, produced the moment that changed the game. Goyal attempted a sweep against Musheer Khan (3/42) but got a top edge. Standing at first slip, Sarfaraz covered the ground towards leg slip, dived full length and completed the catch to end the partnership.The India batter celebrated by running hard and throwing his arm in the air, with his effort even prompting the physio to come onto the field.Mumbai then struck twice more to put the result beyond Railways. India all-rounder Suryansh Shedge ran several yards to his left from mid-off to dismiss Zubair off Musheer, before Tanush Kotian (2/93) took a one-handed catch at short midwicket to remove the eighth batter. Railways were eventually bowled out for 265, with the collapse coming in a frantic final hour after the drinks break.The day had begun with Mumbai adding 60 runs to their overnight lead and setting Railways a target of 372. Divyaansh Saxena, who was unbeaten overnight, remained not out on 100 off 136 balls, hitting eight fours and a six.Railways' chase got off to a difficult start as Shams Mulani (4/69) picked up three wickets and Sarfaraz effected a run-out to leave them at 83/5. Goyal and Zubair then joined forces and appeared to have taken the game towards a draw before Mumbai's late fightback.Mumbai captain Siddesh Lad admitted that the possibility of a draw had crossed their minds, given the team's previous experience in the Irani Cup.“That (a draw) was always on the back of mind, because we had won the first innings and we have bad memories of CCI; we had lost the Irani Trophy on the last day of the match,” Lad told reporters.Mumbai finished the first round with 27 points, the highest tally among all teams. However, Lad said the team was not looking to be satisfied with its performance so far.“Last two seasons (also), we did really well in the league stage. But we don't want to be satisfied with what we have done in the first four games. We have a long journey ahead and we want to do something special -- add something to the legacy of Mumbai this season,” he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Bangladesh hold their breath: Opener Shadman Islam stretchered off after on-field injury in second Test; hosts risk being reduced to 10 players
articles.summary: Bangladesh opener Shadman Islam was stretchered off the field after twisting his ankle while fielding on the second morning of the second Test against
articles.body: Bangladesh opener Shadman Islam was stretchered off the field after twisting his ankle while fielding on the second morning of the second Test against West Indies in Sylhet on Friday.The incident took place in the 78th over of West Indies' first innings when Shadman chased a ball played towards fine leg by Amir Jangoo. The opener slipped while trying to stop the ball and immediately went down in pain near the boundary. He remained on the ground for several minutes before being taken off on a stretcher.Shadman has been taken to hospital for an MRI scan and is currently under observation. A decision on his availability for the remainder of the match will be taken after the scan results.Morning dew had left the outfield wet and slippery near the boundary ropes, The Daily Star reported. Earlier in the day, Bangladesh pacer Hasan Mahmud had also slipped while attempting to stop a delivery."He twisted his left ankle and was taken to hospital for an MRI scan," BCB physio Bayzediul Islam said in a statement.Bangladesh had bowled West Indies out for 356 after lunch on the second day. In Shadman's absence, they sent Nayeem Hasan, who had not batted above No. 8 before this match, to open alongside Tanzid Hasan.Shadman had scored a century in the first Test, but it remains unclear whether he will be able to take any further part in the ongoing match.Bangladesh cannot bring in a concussion substitute if Shadman is ruled out because of the ankle injury, which is unrelated to a head injury. This means they would have to continue with only 10 players for the remainder of the Test.West Indies lead the two-match series 1-0.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Mike Hussey: Australia recruit former Test batter for Ashes preparation
articles.summary: Australia recruit Michael Hussey as a long-term batting consultant to help them prepare for the 2027 Ashes and 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
articles.body:
Australia have recruited Michael Hussey as a long-term batting consultant to help them prepare for the 2027 Ashes and 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

The 51-year-old former batter has been added to the national staff as Australia look to improve their form in the longest format, having drawn 1-1 at home to Bangladesh and then lost 2-1 in South Africa in their past two series.

Hussey served under Stephen Fleming at Indian Premier League side Chennai Super Kings and the new England Test coach was interested in adding him to his coaching team.

However, Australia have now moved to secure their former player on a lengthy deal and Hussey will start work with the national side when they face England in a five-game T20 series from 21 November.

In the T20 format he will help his country prepare for the first Olympic cricket competition in 128 years and the 2028 World Cup, which will be held in Australia and New Zealand in October and November of the same year.

"I am extremely excited about being a part of the team in a more formal and meaningful role in the coming years," Hussey said in a statement.

"This team has achieved so much in recent times, to which I hope I can add value to the coaching and playing groups ahead of what will be an exciting and challenging period."

Australia have suffered a number of poor red-ball batting performances in the last year, starting when two of last winter's Ashes Tests lasted just two days.

They were bowled out for 198 in August as Bangladesh won their first ever Test in Australia , and were dismissed for 99 and 111 in defeats in the second and third Tests against South Africa.

Following the final England T20 on 2 December, they will start a heavy pre-Ashes Test schedule where they will play New Zealand in home for four matches then travel to India for a five-game series.

They then face England in a one-off Test at the Melbourne Cricket Ground from 11 March, celebrating 150 years of Test cricket, and could conceivably reach the World Test Championship final at the Oval on 9 June.

The five-match Ashes series runs from 18 June to 2 August, while Hussey will also work with Australia at the ODI World Cup in South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe in October and November 2027.

Hussey did not play Test cricket until he was a 30-year-old, breaking into the Australia side after the 2005 Ashes and becoming an all-format regular until his international retirement in early 2013.

He played 79 Tests for his country, averaging 51.52 with the bat, and featured in 185 ODIs and 38 T20s, winning the 2007 50-over World Cup and the 2006 and 2009 Champions Trophies.

He is the current head coach of Welsh Fire in the men's Hundred and has served as a short-term batting consultant for Australia on a number of occasions in recent years.

Hussey also worked as a batting consultant for England in 2022, helping them win the T20 World Cup in Australia.

"Mike has been a highly valued part of our staff in the past and brings a considerable skill set which is complementary to the coaches and players," Australia coach Andrew McDonald said.

"Not only is his expertise as a player and coach across multiple formats, competitions, countries invaluable, so are his qualities as a person."

articles.title: 'Clicky Ponting' club cricketer banned for two years after Saltburn cheating scandal
articles.summary: Saltburn Cricket Club confirmed they have been fined £300, while their second XI have been relegated to the third division and will begin next season with a 60-point deduction; Sky Sports News have contacted the north Yorkshire Cricket Board and Saltburn for comment
articles.body:
Brian Devine found himself making headlines across the world this summer when he was caught apparently clicking his fingers at first slip during a match for Saltburn Cricket Club's second XI to trick the umpire into thinking the batsman had edged the ball.

Devine was given the nickname 'Clicky Ponting' in reference to the former Australia captain, Ricky Ponting, with the North Yorkshire and South Durham league launching an investigation.

There were further complaints regarding previous matches and the investigation, which included player interviews, written statements and a detailed review of video footage, took a number of weeks.

Devine and Saltburn admitted the subsequent charges but appealed against the sanction, with a separate panel heard on October 26 and now concluded.

Devine has been suspended from playing, coaching, umpiring, scoring and managing junior teams at all levels until September 29, 2028 while Saltburn have been fined £300.

Their second XI have been relegated to division three of the league and will start the 2027 season with a 60-point deduction. Middlesbrough Cricket Club 2nd XI will retain their place in Division Two.

In a statement reported on gazettelive.co.uk , Saltburn said: "The club fully participated in the disciplinary proceedings and accept the decision of the appeal following the original decision from the league. We are now focusing on preparations for the 2027 season."

In a statement to Sky Sports , the North Yorkshire and South Durham league said: "The league recognises the strain this has placed on many people, especially those who were abused online and in person.

"We ask everyone to respect that the formal process is now complete. The league will make no further comment."

Saltburn Cricket Club found itself under investigation by North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League earlier in the summer after footage of an alleged incident during a second division game against Norton Cricket Club on July 25 went viral.

Norton Cricket Club's Norman Shabir was at the crease and was given out on his first delivery from bowler Sam Morrison.

It appeared to pass by Shabir before travelling to wicketkeeper Josh Bowes, who took the catch.

But just as the ball passed Shabir's bat, Devine, standing at first slip, appears to click his fingers, in an attempt to deceive the umpire the ball had taken a nick off his bat.

Shabir was then given out by the umpire, and proceeded to plead his case with the official before walking off the pitch.

The video has since gained over 7.5m views online and Devine was later dubbed 'Clicky Ponting'.

At the time, Saltburn had been top of the Division Two table, having won 10 of their 15 matches last season.

Earlier in the month, Saltburn sealed a 22-run victory against Shildon Railway Cricket Club. During that match their wicketkeeper took eight catches. No Test wicketkeeper has taken more than seven catches in an innings.

The North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League later launched an investigation.

"This is issued in response to the widely publicised complaint made against a Saltburn Cricket Club member and, as a consequence, against the club more generally," a statement on the league's social media channels read.

"We are treating this allegation with the utmost seriousness and, as a family-centric club, we are fully cooperating with the NYS League's investigation.

"We believe that the club acted decisively as soon as the complaint and investigation were made known to us. The player at the centre of the complaint has been suspended and will not play again for the club this season or in the foreseeable future, pending the outcome of this investigation."

The league later announced that it had met with Saltburn officials and had received guidence from the England and Wales Cricket Board.It also expressed it's "concern for the welfare of those at Saltburn Cricket Club".

When contacted by the Daily Mail , Devine said: "Naturally, I cannot comment on that. I also cannot answer any questions because I am currently at work."

Meanwhile, further footage emerged allegedly showing Devine, playing for Pudsey St Lawrence in the Bradford Premier League, repeatedly clicking his fingers while opposition players were batting.

Pudsey St Lawrence said in a statement on Thursday: "At no stage was the club aware of any alleged misconduct by Mr Devine, nor were any concerns or complaints raised with the club by opposition teams or umpires who officiated the fixtures in question.

"The club expects its players to uphold the highest standards of integrity and sportsmanship and takes any credible concerns extremely seriously."

Banton: 'Clicky Ponting' kind of clever but not acceptable

Speaking on the matter, former England and Somerset player Tom Banton said:

"It's interesting, kind of clever in a way. But I cannot vouch for things like that, it's not acceptable," Banton said.

"It's been caught out and something is going to be done about it because I'm not sure it's in the rules of cricket."

articles.title: Afghanistan Premier League: Female players express disappointment at overseas players' involvement
articles.summary: Afghanistan Refugee Women's cricket team players express disappointment foreign players have signed up for the country's franchise league.
articles.body:
Afghan women's cricketers have accused overseas players signing up for the inaugural Afghanistan Premier League of sending a message to the world that women suffering in the country "can simply be ignored".

Women's participation in sport has been effectively outlawed since the Taliban's return to power in 2021, and many of Afghanistan's female cricketers left the country for their own safety.

The men's franchise league is expected to start in December in the UAE, though it is yet to be sanctioned by the International Cricket Council (ICC).

In September, the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) urged players to reconsider their involvement and batter Ollie Pope withdrew.

"For five years, girls in Afghanistan have been denied the right to play cricket and many other basic rights," Nahida Sapan, who captained the Afghanistan Refugee Women's XI on this summer's tour of England, told the BBC Stumped podcast .

"Foreign players had a real opportunity to stand with millions of Afghan women and girls by choosing not to participate.

"It may have seemed like a small action, but it could have sent a powerful message and put pressure on those responsible.

"This is not about being against cricket or Afghan men's cricket. It is about standing up for basic human rights."

Eight English players were signed in the draft on Tuesday, alongside players from Scotland, Ireland, Australia and New Zealand.

England's Alex Hales, Tymal Mills, Joe Clarke, Olly Stone, Moeen Ali, Luke Wood, Tom Moores and Chris Wood were all signed. Scotland's George Munsey also secured a deal, as did Ireland all-rounder Curtis Campher.

Other England players including Dawid Malan and James Vince also put their names into the draft.

England will have more overseas representation than any other country in the Afghan league.

The major names signed from other nations include Sri Lanka internationals Kusal Perera, Wanindu Hasaranga, Dushmantha Chameera and Kamindu Mendis, Australian batter D'Arcy Short, South Africa spinner Imran Tahir and Bangladesh all-rounder Shakib Al Hasan.

The ECB has refused to schedule bilateral cricket with Afghanistan since the Taliban returned to power - a stance Australia also adopts.

England have, however, continued to play against Afghanistan at global events, including World Cups in both limited-overs formats and the Champions Trophy, which resulted in calls from MPs for their game in 2025 to be boycotted.

"For me, the women and girls of Afghanistan come first," said Sapan. "Their rights, dignity and freedom matter more than any league or sporting opportunity.

"Taking part in this league without acknowledging what is happening to Afghan women risks sending the message to the world that their suffering can simply be ignored."

Afghan women ask ICC for 'clear answers' on future

Afghan women tell the BBC their lives are unrecognisable after five years of Taliban rule

Afghanistan's women's players have repeatedly called on the ICC to recognise them once again as an international team, and commit to long-term funding.

Without official ICC recognition, they play as the Afghan Refugee Women's Team.

In April 2025, the ICC - together with the cricket boards of England, Australia and India - announced a joint programme to provide financial support for the players, and that funding was extended in July.

"To every international player considering participating in this league, I believe there is a responsibility to ask difficult questions," said batter Firooza Amiri.

"You have the freedom to choose where you play, which organisations you represent and which competitions you participate in, but that freedom also comes with a responsibility to understand the systems you may be helping to support.

"I am not asking international players to turn their backs on the people of Afghanistan. I am asking them to recognise the difference between supporting Afghan people and legitimising a system that has systematically taken away women's rights."

Afghanistan men's team has retained full ICC membership despite the country's inability to meet the membership requirement of supporting a women's national side.

Amiri said their stance was not about withdrawing support for the Afghanistan men's team.

"Imagine your daughter, your sister or your wife being told that she cannot attend school simply because she is a woman," she said. "Imagine being told that she cannot play sport, pursue her ambitions or participate in public life.

"We cannot celebrate the development of cricket in Afghanistan while ignoring the complete exclusion of half of its population from the game.

"The question is whether the international cricket community is prepared to stand by its own values when it comes to Afghan women."

articles.title: England Amateur Cricketer Banned 2 Years in Cheating Scandal
articles.summary: LONDON (AP) — An amateur cricketer in England has been banned for two years in a cheating scandal caught on video.
articles.body:
LONDON (AP) — An amateur cricketer in England has been banned for two years in a cheating scandal caught on video.

The allegations came to light in July when a video showed a fielder clicking his fingers to imitate the sound of a bat connecting with the ball before a player is called out.

The North Yorkshire & South Durham Cricket League launched an investigation into the player and the second-division Saltburn team. It spent weeks interviewing players and reviewing video footage.

"Charges were subsequently brought against the player and Saltburn C.C.," the league said in a statement Friday. "Both admitted the charges."

The player, identified across British media as Brian Devine, was suspended from all cricket under the jurisdiction of the England and Wales Cricket Board for a two-year period through late September 2028.

"This covers playing, coaching, umpiring, scoring and managing junior teams," the league said.

The Saltburn team was relegated to division three and will start next season with 60-point deduction. The club also has been fined 300 pounds ($400).

"The league recognizes the strain this has placed on many people, especially those who were abused online and in person. We ask everyone to respect that the formal process is now complete," the league said.

Cricket has had its share of scandals, ranging from the so-called "Sandpapergate" ball-tampering episode in 2018 that led to suspensions for three Australian international players, to spot fixing scandals that have led to lengthy bans.

But at the amateur levels, such as this so-called village cricket competition in England, umpires have no access to video replays to make decisions and there's a level of trust required from players when claiming catches.

A cricket umpire could be fooled into calling a player out if they believed they heard the sound of the ball clipping the edge of a bat before being caught.

British media dubbed the case "Clicky Ponting," a play on the name of Australian great Ricky Ponting.

articles.title: Emerging Nations Trophy: Ireland name two uncapped players for T20 tournament
articles.summary: Ireland name two uncapped players in a 14-strong squad for the Emerging Nations Trophy T20 tournament, with Lara Maritz included after last playing for her country in 2021.
articles.body:
Ireland have named two uncapped players in their squad for the upcoming ICC Emerging Nations Trophy tournament, while Lara Maritz is recalled to international duty five years after she last played for her country.

Seam bowling all-rounder Zara Craig, 23, and wicketkeeper-batter Abbi Harrison, 20, are both called up and will hope to make their first appearances.

Craig plays for Eglinton and Phoenix and has been part of the Irish talent pathway coming up through the underage levels, being a member of the 2023 Women's Under-19s T20 World Cup squad.

Waringstown player Harrison was a member of both the 2023 and 2025 Women's Under-19s T20 World Cup squads.

Twenty-five-year-old all-rounder Maritz has 43 caps to date, making her debut in 2017 and last turning out for Ireland in 2021.

Gaby Lewis will lead the 14-strong squad, with Amy Hunter taking on the vice-captaincy in the absence of Orla Prendergast, who has been granted permission to miss the tournament to participate in the Women's Big Bash League in Australia.

Also missing for Ireland is Rebecca Stokell, who is serving a "voluntary suspension" after taking responsibility for an inadvertent breach of reporting requirements regarding the use of prescription medication.

Leah Paul has made herself unavailable for this tournament, while Christina Coulter Reilly is injured.

Kia McCartney, who has played in five ODIs but has yet to make her Ireland T20I debut, is selected.

The T20I competition will feature 10 teams and will be played in the United Arab Emirates from 12-25 November.

The tournament has been newly expanded to include five Full Members teams and five Associate teams, with Thailand having won the previous edition which involved only Associate nations.

Ireland will face Sri Lanka in their first Group A fixture on 12 November, followed by meetings with Papua New Guinea, UAE and Scotland.

"With no International cricket scheduled until March next year, the timing of the Emerging Nations Trophy provides our Performance Squad with the perfect opportunity to put the learning from the training programmes that have taken place over the last six weeks into high level competition," said Graeme West, Director of High Performance at Cricket Ireland.

"The tournament itself offers our squad the opportunity to take on sides that share a similar goal of entering the top six ranked teams in the world, making for a very competitive event - just what we need as we build towards the next T20 World Cup in 2028."

Ireland squad: Gaby Lewis (c), Amy Hunter (vc), Zara Craig, Alana Dalzell, Laura Delany, Georgina Dempsey, Abbi Harrison, Louise Little, Aimee Maguire, Jane Maguire, Lara Maritz, Lara McBride, Kia McCartney, Cara Murray.

articles.title: ‘Clicky Ponting’ handed two-year suspension over cricket cheating scandal
articles.summary: Amateur cricketer was clicking his fingers while fielding to trick umpire into thinking the batsman had edged the ball.
articles.body:
The English amateur cricketer who went viral ⁠for finger-clicking trickery ⁠has been handed a two-year suspension, the North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League has said.

The fielder Brian Devine, dubbed “Clicky Ponting” on ⁠social media in a nod to former Australia captain Ricky Ponting, was accused of tricking umpires by clicking his fingers to make the ⁠sound of a ball nicking the bat as deliveries were missed and caught by the wicketkeeper.

The video footage went viral on social media and made international headlines earlier this year. A three-person disciplinary panel reviewed the ‌footage and considered player interviews and written statements before imposing the ban.

“The player concerned is suspended from all cricket under the ECB’s [the England and Wales Cricket Board] jurisdiction for two years, from 30 September 2026 to 29 September 2028. This covers playing, coaching, umpiring, scoring and managing junior teams,” the NYSDL said in a statement on Friday.

Additionally, Saltburn ⁠Cricket Club have been fined 300 pounds ($402.87) and ⁠their second XI has been relegated to Division Three of the NYSDCL and will start the 2027 season with a 60-point deduction, the league added.

Devine and Saltburn admitted the charges, but the club appealed against their sanction.

Saltburn said in a statement reported on gazettelive.co.uk: “The club fully participated in the disciplinary proceedings and accept the decision of the appeal following the original decision from the league.”

In a statement to the Press Association, the league said, “The league recognises the strain this has placed on many people, especially those who were abused online and in person.

“We ask everyone to respect that the formal process is now complete. The league will make no further comment.”

Ricky Ponting, who led Australia to two 50-over World Cup titles, told the Reuters news agency that he found ⁠the controversy amusing, although he was less ⁠impressed that his name had become associated with the player.

“I had a bit of a chuckle to myself and pretty much forgot about it after that,” he said in an ‌interview earlier this year.

“I guess it wasn’t a nice thing to have my name associated with someone who’s blatantly cheating but … honestly I ‌had ‌a laugh and a joke about it.”

articles.title: Australia cricket: Usman Khawaja says entire team knew about ball-tampering scandal in South Africa in 2018
articles.summary: Usman Khawaja says “all of us” knew about ‘Sandpapergate’ in Cape Town Test eight years ago and not only Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft as previously asserted by Cricket Australia; former batter speaking ahead of the release his new book
articles.body:
That declaration, made by Khawaja in the Sydney Morning Herald ahead of the release of his book 'Sabr', is at odds with Cricket Australia's assertion that only Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were aware of the plot to use sandpaper on the ball in the third Test against South Africa eight years ago.

Khawaja, who retired from international duty after Australia's 4-1 Ashes thrashing of England last winter, said: "It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us".

Captain-at-the-time Smith, Bancroft and Warner, who was found to have been the architect of the plot, all received bans after the incident, with Smith and Warner suspended for one year and Bancroft handed a nine-month sanction.

Bowlers Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon issued a joint statement in 2021 insisting they had no idea about the ball-tampering.

That came after Bancroft - who had aimed to conceal the sandpaper down his trousers in the Test in question - replied "I think it's probably self-explanatory" when asked whether the bowling attack knew about the scandal.

Khawaja: I thought the truth would have come out by now

Khawaja, who wrote in his book that ball-tampering plans were first discussed in the second Test of the 2018 series in Port Elizabeth, now Gqeberha, continued: "I don't want to be the one who comes out and talks about the truth.

"The issue is that I genuinely thought after eight years the truth would have been out by now.

"Maybe I thought Davey [Warner] would have exposed it, or someone else would have talked about it more.

"At the end of the day, I think it's the right thing to do, particularly for those three guys. And I think most of the guys in the team, at some level, will be relieved that we can finally move on."

"Even in the change rooms when I was talking to them after the game. I said: 'Take this as a team. We did this as a team. We knew what was going on. We have to take it as a team'.

"I was always of that stance. Obviously, it didn't work that way, and those three guys got crucified".

articles.title: Sandpapergate: Usman Khawaja claims whole Australia team knew about use of sandpaper to tamper with ball against South Africa
articles.summary: Usman Khawaja claims the entire Australia team knew about the use of sandpaper to tamper with the ball in the final Test of their 2018 series with South Africa.
articles.body:
Usman Khawaja has claimed the entire Australia team knew about the use of sandpaper to tamper with the ball in the final Test of their 2018 series with South Africa.

In extracts of his autobiography - Sabr - published in the Sydney Morning Herald, , external the former opening batter said Australia had also used the ball-tampering tactic in the Test before the infamous match in Cape Town.

The incident - nicknamed 'sandpapergate' - was widely condemned and led to bans for captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and fellow batter Cameron Bancroft.

"It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us," Khawaja, 39, told the Sydney Morning Herald.

The four Australia bowlers who played in that match, including current Test captain Pat Cummins, have consistently denied they had any prior knowledge of the plan.

In 2021, Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon issued a joint statement saying they "did not know a foreign substance was taken on to the field".

Khawaja, who scored 6,229 runs in 88 Tests, said that discussions about tampering with the ball began during the second Test of the series against South Africa.

That match, played at Port Elizabeth - now Gqeberha - led to what Khawaja said was the "discovery of sandpaper as an effective agent" after "open" discussions held in the dressing room at St George's Park.

"At this point Smith essentially threw his hands in the air and said he didn't want to know," Khawaja wrote.

Australia were rumbled in the third Test when television cameras clearly showed Bancroft using sandpaper on the ball to help generate reverse swing.

Khawaja was also shocked not to be asked to provide any evidence during Cricket Australia's investigation.

"In an ideal world, I don't want to do this. I don't want to be the one who comes out and talks about the truth," he said.

"The issue is that I genuinely thought after eight years the truth would have been out by now."

While Smith, Warner and Bancroft - all batters - were punished, there was never an explanation of how bowlers Cummins, Starc, Hazlewood and Lyon did not notice a change in the state of the ball.

In a 2021 interview with the Guardian, Bancroft was asked if the bowlers knew and replied: "It's pretty probably self-explanatory."

Days after Bancroft's interview was published, the quartet released their statement which said: "We feel compelled to put the key facts on the record again.

"We did not know a foreign substance was taken on to the field to alter the condition of the ball until we saw the images on the big screen at Newlands.

"And to those who, despite the absence of evidence, insist that 'we must have known' about the use of a foreign substance simply because we are bowlers, we say this: The umpires during that Test match, Nigel Llong and Richard Illingworth, both very respected and experienced umpires, inspected the ball after the images surfaced on the TV coverage and did not change it because there was no sign of damage.

"We respectfully request an end to the rumour-mongering and innuendo. It has gone on too long and it is time to move on."

Before Australia's recent Test series in South Africa - which the Proteas won 2-1 - Cummins said he had spoken to Khawaja about the publication of the book.

The 33-year-old said he has no concerns about potential sandpapergate revelations and felt it was "all dealt with then" and the team had "moved on".

"He didn't go into too much detail, just basically gave me the heads-up that he is doing a book and, as always, no worries," Cummins said on 8 October.

"Tell your story. It's fine. It's obviously a long time ago and all the investigations, everything was done back then and we answered every question a million times."

Khawaja also said he had consistently argued that the team should take responsibility together, including in the dressing room after the Cape Town Test.

He wrote: "I said: 'Take this as a team. We did this as a team. We knew what was going on, and we have to take it as a team'.

"Obviously, it didn't work that way, and those three guys got crucified."

In his memoir, named after an Arabic term for resilience and endurance, Khawaja dedicated the chapter on Cape Town to Smith, Warner and Bancroft.

The left-handed batter said he thought the trio "deserve" the "justice" of collective blame from the team as a whole.

He added: "None of those three want to be the first to say anything. And rightly so, it will just be hearsay and 'their word' if they do. They needed someone else to say something.

"But I'm not doing this for any other reason than I think it's the right thing to do."

articles.title: Not an easy task to be coach of the Indian cricket team: Kyle Mills
articles.summary: Wellington: India under head coach Gautam Gambhir has undergone a massive transition in Test cricket but continues to enjoy some stability in the ODI
articles.body: Wellington: India under head coach Gautam Gambhir has undergone a massive transition in Test cricket but continues to enjoy some stability in the ODI format. The presence of senior players Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma, KL Rahul and Shreyas Iyer has kept the core intact for captain Shubman Gill as the team firms up its plans for the 2027 World Cup, with the ongoing ODI series against New Zealand.In an exclusive chat with TOI, former New Zealand bowler Kyle Mills opens up about coach Gambhir and the scrutiny his team faces, the changing scene in New Zealand cricket and the reasons for their recent domination.ExcerptsHow do you think India under Gautam Gambhir are shaping up?He's [Gambhir] always been a tough competitor on the field, without question. No jokes were going around at all because he always meant business on the field. Post-retirement, he entered politics and became a leader. A great tactician, a wonderful player, very professional across all facets of the game, and a tough taskmaster as well. He's a tough guy.Do you think the scrutiny is fair when results go wrong?I actually wouldn't think of another sporting team that faces as much scrutiny as the Indian cricket team, across all sports. Obviously, Manchester United have had their challenges in recent years and you've got these big teams around the world like the New York Yankees and the All Blacks, but the Indian cricket team certainly gets scrutinised, and Gambhir is the leader of that. So, it's not an easy task to be coach of the Indian cricket team, but he always has the bit between his teeth, and he's a tough customer.One last dance for Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma on New Zealand soil. Are you looking forward to seeing them in action?It's going to be a joy to have them here because they're two wonderful cricketers, and Rohit Sharma is always a cricketer that you actually like watching bat. I think it's a term that often gets used about Rohit, that he has more time than others, but the reality is he has the same amount of time as everyone else, but he just makes it look easy. Would have loved to see the two of them here for red-ball cricket too.India are now transitioning into the Shubman Gill era. What has been your first impression?I think he's a beautiful player. He's got all the strokes. He's a very charismatic guy. Sport's a funny game. You never own the shirt. You never own the cap. There are always people just passing through it. You think of Sachin Tendulkar. Go back to Gavaskar [Sunil], Kapil Dev. Then you go to the likes of Laxman, Dravid, Tendulkar. They all just travel through this team, and then there's been Virat and Rohit, and now they've had their turn and now we're into a new generation, and that's the beauty of sport.And the IPL continues to ensure a seamless transition...The IPL has done wonders, absolute wonders for the game in India, especially in white-ball cricket. You've got not just your star Indian players, but your second-, third-, fourth- and probably fifth-rated players being exposed to international cricketers in the IPL, so that advances their development.
